paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when you're outnumbered, you pray before you panic. Jehoshaphat was alarmed, and he still set his face to seek the LORD (2 Chronicles 20:3). Then he said it out loud in front of everybody: "We do not know what to do, but our eyes are upon You." (2 Chronicles 20:12) I can't admit a burnt batch without blaming the oven, and that king admitted he was powerless in front of a whole crowd!

Then comes the line to hang on your fridge. Through Jahaziel, the LORD says, "Do not be afraid or discouraged because of this vast army, for the battle does not belong to you, but to God." (2 Chronicles 20:15) Judah still had to show up. They got up early, they believed, and they went out singing, "Give thanks to the LORD, for His loving devotion endures forever." (2 Chronicles 20:21) Your battle might be a bill, a diagnosis, or a boss, and the same God is still worth thanking before the answer shows up.

Now, the story doesn't end on a perfect note, and I think that's on purpose. The high places stayed, and the people had not yet set their hearts on the God of their fathers (2 Chronicles 20:33). Then Jehoshaphat allied himself with Ahaziah, and his ships were wrecked (2 Chronicles 20:35-37). So keep leaning on the LORD after the victory party, friend, because that's when we get comfortable.
